supports_claims: Training LLMs with stepwise self-correction can improve robustness to noisy retrieved documents in RAG without requiring extensive external annotations. | Reformulating RAG as a multi-step decision-making process with backtracking enables models to better assess document relevance and avoid being misled by irrelevant evidence.
rationale: The paper proposes Backtracking Correction, a method that trains LLMs to perform stepwise assessment of retrieved documents to handle noisy or irrelevant evidence in RAG. It directly compares Label-Supervised Tuning and Chain-Supervised Tuning approaches, identifying limitations in how models distinguish relevant from irrelevant documents. This is highly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence, particularly for the model-side evidence use dimension. Published at ICLR 2025 with code available, it constitutes a useful method lineage citation for the survey.
caveat: Method evaluated only on open-domain QA datasets with relatively short documents; generalization to other RAG scenarios like long-context or multimodal is not validated.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
supports_claims: Self-synthesized rationales can train LMs to explicitly denoise noisy retrieved contexts, improving robustness to imperfect retrievers. | Explicit rationale-based denoising scales better with more retrieved documents than vanilla RAG, mitigating performance degradation under high noise ratios. | Instruction-tuning-style rationale supervision generalizes across in-domain and out-of-domain RAG tasks without extra human annotation.
rationale: InstructRAG proposes a self-synthesized rationale framework that teaches LMs to explicitly distinguish useful from noisy retrieved documents and justify answers, directly addressing the unreliable-evidence problem central to the survey. It offers both training-free ICL and supervised fine-tuning variants, with experiments showing improved robustness under increased noise ratios across five QA benchmarks. As an ICLR 2025 paper with code and strong empirical denoising results, it is a backbone reference for the model-side evidence-use perspective. Risk of overclaiming is modest since experiments focus on QA-style tasks and rely on pattern-matching evaluation supplemented by LLM-as-judge.
caveat: Evaluation is largely confined to QA benchmarks and depends on substring/LLM-judge metrics; generalization to open-ended generation or adversarial poisoning is not directly tested.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
supports_claims: Unifying context reranking with answer generation in a single instruction-tuned LLM improves robustness to noisy retrieved contexts. | A small fraction of ranking data integrated into instruction tuning can outperform dedicated rerankers trained on much larger ranking corpora. | Reranking the top-N retrieved passages to a refined top-k mitigates the recall-vs-noise trade-off that hurts generation quality.
rationale: RankRAG instruction-tunes a single LLM to jointly perform context ranking and answer generation, explicitly targeting the failure mode where retrievers return irrelevant or noisy passages that mislead generation. It is directly relevant to evidence construction for robust RAG, with strong empirical results across nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks plus biomedical tasks, and includes ablations showing the reranking step is essential. As a NeurIPS 2024 venue paper that establishes a method lineage for retrieve-rerank-generate pipelines, it is a natural main-text citation under evidence construction.
caveat: Focuses on single-round retrieval with text-only QA; does not address multimodal evidence, adversarial poisoning, or calibrated abstention, so should not be overclaimed as a general robustness solution.
notes: HuggingFace link in text refers to MedRAG corpus, not the RankRAG model itself.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
supports_claims: LLMs often over-rely on external context regardless of factual accuracy, motivating situated faithfulness that dynamically balances internal knowledge with external evidence. | Self-guided and rule-based confidence reasoning, especially when trained via CR-DPO, can improve robustness to incorrect retrieved contexts and generalize across QA datasets including the new RedditQA benchmark of human-written misleading posts.
rationale: The paper directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable evidence by benchmarking LLMs under knowledge conflicts with both LLM-synthesized and human-written incorrect contexts (RedditQA), and proposes SCR, RCR, and CR-DPO methods to enhance situated faithfulness. It contributes a clear taxonomy of confidence reasoning strategies, an evaluation protocol (Acc_t, Acc_f, SF), and a new dataset with verified noisy contexts, all of which are core to a survey on robust RAG. Main-text citation under model_evidence_use is appropriate because the work centers on grounding, faithfulness, and knowledge conflict resolution rather than retrieval or security per se.
caveat: Focuses on short-form QA with a single context per instance; multi-document retrieval and long-form generation conflicts are not directly evaluated.
notes: Could also be cited under action_control for CR-DPO and confidence calibration aspects; RedditQA is a useful evaluation artifact.

title: xRAG: Extreme Context Compression for Retrieval-augmented Generation with One Token
supports_claims: Extreme context compression via modality fusion can preserve RAG performance while reducing inference cost. | Self-distillation training can improve robustness to noisy or misleading retrieved evidence, as measured by resilience and boost rates.
rationale: xRAG compresses a retrieved document into a single token via a projector that maps dense retriever embeddings into the LLM representation space, trained with paraphrase pretraining and context-aware instruction tuning including self-distillation. It is directly relevant to robust RAG because it introduces instance-level robustness metrics (Resilience Rate, Boost Rate) and demonstrates better robustness than RAG to misleading or irrelevant retrieved documents. Suitable as a main citation under evidence construction/compression, with secondary value for evaluation and model evidence use.
caveat: Robustness gains may partly stem from underuse of compressed context (lower boost rate on multi-hop tasks), so claims about robustness should be balanced with reasoning limitations.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
supports_claims: RAG knowledge bases and agent long-term memory can be poisoned with <0.1% malicious instances to reliably trigger adversarial actions while preserving benign utility. | Constrained trigger optimization that maps triggered queries to a unique, compact embedding region transfers across dense retrievers and resists perplexity-based and rephrasing defenses. | Backdoor and poisoning threats are especially severe for RAG-based agents in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving and healthcare.
rationale: AgentPoison is a NeurIPS 2024 paper that introduces the first backdoor attack specifically targeting RAG-based LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge base, providing a novel constrained optimization to ensure malicious demonstrations are retrieved for triggered queries. It directly illustrates how unreliable/manipulated evidence stores can compromise RAG pipelines and induce adversarial agent actions, making it core material for the survey's security/integrity discussion of unreliable evidence. The empirical evaluation across three real agents, transferability analyses, and defense study give it strong evidentiary value for main-text discussion. The main caveat is that it assumes white-box access to the embedder for trigger optimization, though transferability mitigates this.
caveat: Attack assumes white-box access to the RAG embedder for trigger optimization; defense coverage is limited to perplexity filter and rephrasing baselines.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Iterative chain-of-retrieval with learned query reformulation improves robustness when single-step retrieval fails on complex multi-hop queries. | Test-time compute can be adaptively scaled (chain length, best-of-N, tree search, learning-to-stop) to control the trade-off between answer quality and retrieval reliability. | Trained iterative retrievers remain robust across retrievers of varying quality (E5-large, E5-base, BM25), indicating partial decoupling from retriever noise.
rationale: CoRAG explicitly trains an LLM via rejection-sampled retrieval chains to decompose queries, reformulate when retrieval fails, and decide when to stop, which is directly aligned with action-control and adaptive retrieval under unreliable evidence. It also offers concrete test-time decoding strategies and a learning-to-stop mechanism that map to abstention/routing themes in the survey. Robustness experiments across different retrievers and recall improvements on multi-hop QA make it a strong venue-linked backbone reference. Overclaim risk is modest since gains are marginal on single-hop tasks like NQ, which the authors note.
caveat: Focuses on short-answer multi-hop QA and KILT tasks; does not directly evaluate adversarial or poisoned evidence, and benefits diminish on simple single-hop queries.
notes: NeurIPS 2025; code at microsoft/LMOps/corag.

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Mechanistic interventions on FFN activations can mitigate over-reliance on parametric memory and improve contextual faithfulness in RAG. | Benchmarks like CoFaithfulQA enable evaluation of LLM faithfulness under realistic conflicts between internal knowledge and accurate retrieved evidence.
rationale: ParamMute identifies a subset of mid-to-deep FFN layers causally implicated in unfaithful RAG generation and suppresses them, combined with preference optimization to calibrate the model toward retrieved evidence. It also introduces CoFaithfulQA, a benchmark built from six QA datasets that captures realistic context-vs-memory conflicts, and reports results on ConFiQA and FaithEval. This directly contributes to the survey's themes of faithfulness, knowledge conflict, and grounding under retrieved evidence, making it a strong main-text citation for the model evidence use perspective.
caveat: Evaluation focuses on QA settings with text contexts and a limited set of backbone models; mechanism-level claims about UA-FFNs may not generalize to all architectures or modalities.
notes: Could also be cross-referenced in evaluation section due to CoFaithfulQA benchmark contribution.

title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
supports_claims: Retrieval augmentation can degrade RALM performance when retrieved contexts are irrelevant, especially in multi-hop reasoning where errors cascade. | NLI-based filtering with a back-off to no-retrieval generation is an effective training-free method to mitigate harm from irrelevant evidence, but it over-discards relevant passages. | Fine-tuning with a small mixture of relevant and irrelevant retrieved contexts (as few as 1,000 examples) yields RALMs robust to noisy retrieval while preserving gains from useful evidence.
rationale: The paper provides a systematic analysis of RALM brittleness to irrelevant retrieved context across five ODQA benchmarks (including multi-hop) and proposes two complementary remedies: an NLI-based filter with back-off and a data-efficient fine-tuning recipe mixing relevant and noisy contexts. Both contributions directly target the survey's core themes of unreliable evidence robustness, model evidence use, and action control via abstention/back-off. Publication at ICLR 2024 with released code, data, and models makes it a backbone reference for the model-side handling of unreliable retrieval, suitable for the main model-use section.
caveat: Experiments are limited to ODQA with Llama-2-13B/70B and small training sets; generalization to other modalities, domains, or larger retrieval corpora is not fully established.

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
supports_claims: Dense retrievers used in domain-specific RAG are universally vulnerable to corpus poisoning that appends targeted content to attacker-chosen queries, with high top-K retrieval success across corpora, retrievers, and queries. | An orthogonal augmentation property of dense retrievers explains why poisoned concatenated documents retain high similarity to queries, motivating distribution-aware (Mahalanobis-style) detection defenses that outperform L2-norm baselines.
rationale: The paper provides a large-scale empirical study (225 setups in medical Q&A plus legal Q&A) showing dense retrievers can be reliably manipulated via concatenation-based poisoning, and offers a mechanistic explanation via the orthogonal augmentation property and low query-document similarity. It then proposes a shrinkage-regularized Mahalanobis detector that achieves near-perfect detection across attacks including PoisonedRAG. These are directly aligned with the survey's security/integrity and unreliable-evidence themes, making it a main citation under the security perspective with domain-specific scenario coverage.
caveat: Focus is mainly on retrieval-stage poisoning detection; downstream LLM generation robustness and adaptive attackers against the proposed detector are not deeply evaluated.
notes: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); no explicit code/data link found in extracted text.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
supports_claims: RAG datastores are vulnerable to prompt-injection-based extraction attacks that exploit instruction-following capabilities of LMs. | Position bias and ineffective context utilization are root causes of datastore leakage, and position-invariant inference combined with safety-aware prompting mitigates the attack. | Production RAG systems such as customized GPTs can leak verbatim datastore content at high rates with minimal queries.
rationale: This ICLR 2025 paper systematically studies prompt-injection-based data extraction from RIC-style RAG systems across many open-weights LMs and production GPTs, quantifying leakage rates, identifying instruction tuning and position bias as drivers, and proposing PINE plus safety-aware prompts as defenses. It is a strong fit for the security/integrity dimension of a robust RAG survey because it characterizes a concrete unreliable-evidence threat (adversarial context manipulation) and reliability/defense mechanisms. Main-cite placement under security is appropriate, with low overclaim risk since the empirical scope and threat model are explicit.
caveat: Focus is on datastore privacy leakage rather than answer correctness under noisy/poisoned evidence, so framing should not overextend it to general retrieval noise robustness.
notes: Code link referenced in abstract; PINE defense ties to position-bias literature relevant to evidence use.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Context Compression and Selective Augmentation
supports_claims: Context compression of retrieved documents into concise summaries can reduce distraction from irrelevant evidence while preserving task performance. | Selective augmentation, where the compressor can output an empty summary when retrieval is unhelpful, mitigates the harm of irrelevant or noisy retrieved documents. | End-task-signal-trained extractive and abstractive compressors transfer across LMs and outperform off-the-shelf summarizers as evidence filters.
rationale: RECOMP introduces extractive and abstractive compressors trained with end-task signals to summarize retrieved documents, explicitly handling cases where retrieval is irrelevant or unhelpful by emitting empty summaries (selective augmentation). This directly targets robust RAG under unreliable evidence by filtering noise and reducing distraction, supported by analyses on QA and language modeling. It is a venue-published (ICLR 2024) backbone reference for evidence construction and context compression with reliability-oriented design. Overclaim risk is modest: selective augmentation F1 versus oracle is limited and transfer to other LMs (e.g., LLaMA) is imperfect.
caveat: Selective augmentation accuracy is modest versus oracle, and abstractive compressors can still hallucinate or drop information, especially for multi-hop tasks like HotpotQA.
notes: Strong fit for evidence_construction section; also relevant secondary discussion under action_control for selective augmentation.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
supports_claims: Reliability-aware document filtering using contradiction graphs and Maximum Independent Set provides provable robustness against bounded retrieval corruption in RAG | Leveraging retriever-provided ranking or cardinal reliability signals enables a defense-in-depth approach against prompt injection and corpus poisoning attacks | Weighted sample-and-aggregate frameworks can scale robust RAG defenses to larger retrieval sets while preserving robustness guarantees
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper proposes ReliabilityRAG, a defense framework against adversarial attacks on RAG retrieval corpora using NLI-based contradiction detection and Maximum Independent Set selection that prioritizes higher-ranked documents. It provides both provable robustness guarantees and empirical evaluation against prompt injection and corpus poisoning, comparing favorably to RobustRAG, AstuteRAG, and InstructRAG on QA and long-form generation tasks. The work directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable/adversarial evidence and is a strong venue-backbone citation for the security/integrity perspective with explicit attention to retrieval reliability signals.
caveat: Defense effectiveness depends on NLI model accuracy and assumes bounded corruption; the consistent-majority assumption may not hold for ambiguous queries, and code was not released at submission time.
notes: Closely linked to RobustRAG lineage; useful for both security and evidence-construction discussion.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
supports_claims: Multimodal RAG systems suffer from attention bias toward visual tokens and knowledge conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge, requiring adaptive mechanisms to balance the two when retrieved evidence varies in reliability. | Training-free decoding interventions that adaptively reweight parametric vs contextual logits based on attention-derived reliability signals can mitigate unreliable retrieval in MLLMs.
rationale: ALFAR is a NeurIPS 2025 multimodal RAG method that directly addresses two core robust-RAG problems: knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved context, and attention bias that limits effective use of retrieved evidence. It uses retrieval similarity and query-context relevance to adaptively shift attention and fuse logits, explicitly handling the case when contextual knowledge is unreliable. This makes it a strong fit for the multimodal scenario chapter and for the model-evidence-use discussion of how MLLMs handle noisy context.
caveat: Method is decoding-only and assumes white-box access to MLLM parameters; evaluation focuses on knowledge-intensive VQA benchmarks rather than adversarial or poisoned retrieval settings.
notes: Strong fit as a multimodal RAG case for handling unreliable retrieved evidence via adaptive logits fusion.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic  Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
supports_claims: Two-stage semantic and conflict-aware filtering can defend RAG against corpus poisoning while preserving useful evidence. | Structured semantic extraction (entities, intent, relations) enables fine-grained detection of poisoned or conflicting retrieved documents. | Joint clustering plus semantic-graph filtering with conflict-aware inference reduces attack success rate across multiple LLMs and QA benchmarks.
rationale: SeCon-RAG proposes a two-stage defense (SCF + CAF) explicitly targeting corpus poisoning and prompt injection in RAG, combining clustering-based filtering, EIRE-guided semantic graph filtering, and inference-time conflict resolution across query/corpus/model knowledge. It is directly aligned with the survey's focus on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, providing both a security-integrity defense and an action-control-adjacent mechanism for resolving knowledge conflicts. The NeurIPS 2025 venue, evaluation across five LLMs and three QA datasets, and comparison with TrustRAG/AstuteRAG/InstructRAG make it a strong backbone citation for the security/defense section.
caveat: Relies on a small manually curated set of verified clean documents and multiple LLM calls, which may limit scalability and reproducibility; code availability is stated but artifact link is not clearly verified.
notes: Useful for cross-referencing with TrustRAG, AstuteRAG, RobustRAG, and InstructRAG in the defenses-against-poisoning lineage.

title: StructRAG: Boosting Knowledge Intensive Reasoning of LLMs via Inference-time Hybrid Information Structurization
supports_claims: Restructuring scattered evidence into task-appropriate structured forms (tables, graphs, catalogues, algorithms, chunks) improves RAG over noisy long-context inputs. | A learned routing module that selects the optimal evidence structure type per task can reduce reasoning errors caused by dispersed, noisy retrieved chunks. | Hybrid evidence structurization outperforms single-format approaches (e.g., chunk-only RAG, GraphRAG) on knowledge-intensive multi-document reasoning.
rationale: StructRAG proposes inference-time hybrid information structurization for RAG, comprising a DPO-trained router that picks among five structural formats, an LLM-based structurizer, and a utilizer that decomposes questions and extracts precise knowledge. The paper directly addresses unreliable evidence problems—scattered, noisy retrievals over very long multi-document inputs (up to 200K tokens)—and shows performance gains grow as evidence becomes more dispersed (Loong sets 1-4). It belongs in the evidence-construction section of the survey since it provides a concrete mechanism for converting raw retrieval into more reliable structured context, with ablations isolating router/structurizer/utilizer contributions.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to Loong and one summarization benchmark with Qwen2 backbones; exact-match drops are acknowledged due to format loss during structurization, and robustness to adversarial or counterfactual evidence is not directly tested.
notes: Code available at https://github.com/icip-cas/StructRAG; ICLR 2025 publication.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
supports_claims: Defining and detecting context sufficiency is a key lens for diagnosing RAG failures under unreliable evidence. | LLMs frequently hallucinate rather than abstain when retrieved context is insufficient, motivating action-control mechanisms. | Selective generation combining sufficient-context signals with model confidence improves accuracy-coverage trade-offs in RAG.
rationale: The paper introduces a formal notion of sufficient context and an LLM-based autorater to classify (query, context) pairs, then uses it to diagnose RAG failures across multiple SOTA models and benchmarks. It demonstrates that models hallucinate more than they abstain under insufficient context and proposes a selective generation method combining sufficiency and confidence signals to reduce hallucinations by 2-10%. This directly contributes both an evidence-quality diagnostic and an action-control mechanism central to a robust RAG survey, making it a backbone citation. The placement under evidence construction reflects the core sufficient-context contribution, though it could equally anchor action_control discussion.
caveat: Analysis is limited to QA datasets and does not cover summarization or multimodal RAG; autorater accuracy (93%) introduces some labeling noise in downstream claims.
notes: Bridges evidence sufficiency and selective generation; could also be cited in main:control section.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
supports_claims: Vision-language retrieval over document page images (ColPali with late interaction) provides a simpler and more robust evidence-construction pipeline for visually rich RAG, avoiding brittle OCR/layout/captioning steps. | The ViDoRe benchmark enables evaluation of multimodal document retrieval across domains, languages, and visual element types, supporting reliability assessment of visual RAG pipelines.
rationale: ColPali (ICLR 2025) is a venue-backbone work for multimodal/visual document retrieval, directly relevant to the modality-scenario chapter of a robust RAG survey. It replaces fragile multi-stage OCR/parsing/captioning pipelines (a key source of unreliable textual evidence) with end-to-end VLM-based multi-vector retrieval and introduces ViDoRe as an evaluation benchmark. Both the method and benchmark are widely adopted reference points for visual RAG evidence construction. Overclaim risk is modest if positioned narrowly as evidence-construction for visual RAG rather than as a general robustness mechanism against adversarial or conflicting evidence.
caveat: The paper focuses on retrieval quality/latency, not explicitly on noise robustness, knowledge conflict, or abstention; cite for evidence-construction in visual RAG, not for reliability claims.
notes: Strong artifact availability (HuggingFace models, data, leaderboard); useful as canonical citation for vision-based document RAG.

title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
supports_claims: Test-time critique-driven refinement can correct reasoning misalignment between LLM outputs and retrieved evidence, improving faithfulness under noisy retrieval. | Training a dedicated Critic Language Model via contrastive critique synthesis mitigates self-bias and outperforms larger self-critic baselines. | Dynamic stopping mechanisms (autonomous variants) enable adaptive refinement steps without sacrificing accuracy, addressing efficiency-robustness tradeoffs in RAG.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper reframes RAG as Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning and explicitly tackles reasoning misalignment between LLM outputs and retrieved evidence via a learned Critic Language Model trained with contrastive critique synthesis, then iteratively refines outputs at test time. The work directly targets reliability under noisy/informative retrieval scenarios with empirical evaluation across seven QA benchmarks and three model families, making it strong evidence for the model-evidence-use perspective of robust RAG. It also includes an action-control element through AlignRAG-auto's dynamic stopping. The main-text placement under model evidence use is appropriate, with secondary relevance to action control.
caveat: The 'robustness to noisy retrieval' claims are mostly QA-focused and the failure analysis shows the critic can hallucinate when retrieval is incomplete, so survey should not overclaim general robustness beyond QA settings.
notes: Published at NeurIPS 2025; code released on GitHub per abstract.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-trained adaptive search intensity scaling enables LLMs to escalate retrieval depth and frequency when facing noisy or unreliable open-web evidence | Real-world open-web RAG benchmarks (WebPuzzle) elicit information-seeking behaviors such as conflict resolution, verification, and reflection that clean Wiki-based benchmarks under-test
rationale: The paper proposes DeepDiver, an RL framework that learns adaptive search intensity (when and how much to retrieve) for iterative RAG in noisy real-world web environments, and introduces WebPuzzle, a benchmark explicitly designed around unreliable and conflicting evidence. This directly contributes to robust RAG via action control (adaptive retrieval/abstention from over-confident answering) and to evaluation under unreliable evidence, making it suitable as a main citation in the action-control section with secondary relevance to evaluation. The overclaim risk is modest since experiments are limited to 7B models and Chinese-centric data, but the mechanism and benchmark are clearly venue-published and methodologically supportive of the survey.
caveat: Experiments are constrained to 7B backbones and a primarily Chinese open-web setting; generalization claims to English/larger models rely on translated subsets.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper; code/data not yet released at submission time per checklist.

title: Trustworthy Alignment of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-based alignment can train retrieval-augmented LLMs to prioritize retrieved context over parametric memory in knowledge-conflict settings | Reward shaping with KL and anti-collapse penalties enables trustworthy grounding without explicit supervision on how to respond
rationale: The paper proposes Trustworthy-Alignment, a PPO-based RL method that rewards retrieval-augmented LLMs for generating responses grounded in retrieved evidence and penalizes reliance on parametric knowledge under counterfactual conflicts. It provides theoretical convergence analysis and demonstrates generalization across Natural Questions, ConflictQA-PopQA, and ConflictQA-StrategyQA, making it directly relevant to the model-evidence-use axis of robust RAG. Placement under main:model is appropriate because it represents a method lineage for resolving knowledge conflicts and improving context faithfulness.
caveat: Assumes retrieved evidence contains the correct answer; performance depends on inherent instruction-following capacity of base model and may not handle imperfect retrieval well without modification.
notes: ICML 2024 venue-published, code available on GitHub

title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
supports_claims: Vision-language RAG systems can be compromised by injecting a single optimized poison image-text pair into the multimodal knowledge database, demonstrating a key unreliable-evidence threat in multimodal RAG. | Existing defenses such as noise addition, random cropping, and RoCLIP rematching are insufficient against optimized cross-modal poisoning attacks, motivating dedicated robustness mechanisms for VLRAG. | The retrieval stage is the primary attack surface in VLRAG: once the poison sample is retrieved, the LVLM is highly likely to generate the attacker's target response.
rationale: This ICML 2025 paper presents the first knowledge poisoning attack tailored to vision-language RAG, introducing three progressively stronger variants (baseline, single-query targeted, and class-query targeted) that manipulate VLRAG outputs via a single injected image-text pair. It directly supports the security/integrity strand of a robust RAG survey by characterizing how unreliable multimodal evidence can be inserted, retrieved, and weaponized, and it empirically shows that standard defenses (noise, crop, RoCLIP) only partially mitigate the threat. Placement in main:security is appropriate because it is a venue-backbone reference for the multimodal poisoning subarea and complements text-only attacks like PoisonedRAG, TrojanRAG, and AgentPoison.
caveat: Focus is on attack design with limited evaluation of defenses; claims about robustness implications should be framed as motivating, not solving, multimodal RAG defense.
notes: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); first VLRAG poisoning attack — natural multimodal counterpart to PoisonedRAG for the security section.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Knowledge-graph-based indexing with Personalized PageRank enables single-step multi-hop retrieval, improving evidence integration across passages compared to standard dense retrieval. | Graph-structured evidence construction can outperform iterative retrieval (e.g., IRCoT) on multi-hop QA while being substantially cheaper and faster.
rationale: HippoRAG proposes a neurobiologically inspired RAG framework that builds an open KG from a corpus via LLM-driven OpenIE and uses Personalized PageRank for retrieval, enabling cross-passage knowledge integration in a single retrieval step. It is directly relevant to the evidence-construction axis of a robust-RAG survey as a representative graph/KG-based retrieval method with strong multi-hop QA results at NeurIPS 2024. It does not directly target unreliable evidence (noise, conflict, poisoning), so its role in the survey is primarily as evidence-construction lineage and a scenario example for graph-based RAG rather than a robustness method per se.
caveat: The paper focuses on multi-hop knowledge integration rather than unreliable-evidence robustness; overclaiming its relevance to noise/conflict/attack resilience should be avoided.
notes: Influential NeurIPS 2024 work; code and data available on GitHub.

title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text
supports_claims: MuRAG extends retrieval-augmented generation to multimodal memory by jointly indexing images and text, enabling answers to visual information-seeking queries that text-only RAG cannot address. | Joint contrastive and generative pre-training over image-text and text-only corpora improves both retrieval and grounded generation in multimodal QA. | Error analysis reveals shortcut learning where the model relies on textual clues rather than visual grounding, highlighting a robustness/faithfulness gap in multimodal RAG.
rationale: MuRAG is a foundational EMNLP 2022 paper introducing a multimodal retrieval-augmented transformer that retrieves over image-text memory using a ViT+T5 backbone with contrastive+generative training, evaluated on WebQA and MultimodalQA. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, this is a canonical backbone reference for the multimodal/vision scenario section, and its error analysis (counting, recognition errors, shortcut learning when retrieval is wrong but answer happens to be right via text shortcuts) is directly relevant to faithfulness/grounding under unreliable evidence. Placement in main:modality is appropriate as it anchors the multimodal RAG lineage. Overclaim risk is low if presented as a method/scenario foundation rather than a robustness solution.
caveat: The paper focuses on accuracy and pre-training design, not explicit defenses against noisy or adversarial evidence; robustness claims should be limited to its qualitative observations of shortcut learning.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
supports_claims: Multimodal medical RAG can be made robust by combining domain-aware retrieval, adaptive context selection, and preference fine-tuning that targets cross-modality and over-reliance misalignment. | RAG can degrade Med-LVLM behavior by inducing copy-reference and over-reliance on retrieved text; preference data construction explicitly addressing these failure modes mitigates them. | Adaptive truncation of retrieved contexts based on similarity score gaps improves factuality over fixed-k retrieval in medical VQA and report generation.
rationale: MMed-RAG is a venue-published (ICLR 2025) multimodal RAG system that explicitly diagnoses and mitigates two reliability failure modes when evidence is unreliable: cross-modality misalignment (model ignoring the image and copying retrieved text) and over-reliance (incorrect retrieved context overriding correct internal knowledge). It contributes adaptive context selection, domain-aware retrieval, and RAG-based preference fine-tuning with theoretical analysis, all directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence in a multimodal medical scenario. Placement in main:modality is appropriate as a backbone example of multimodal/domain-specific robust RAG; it also supports evidence_construction and model_evidence_use claims.
caveat: Scope is limited to medical vision-language tasks with yes/no VQA and report generation; generalization claims to broader multimodal RAG settings should be made cautiously.
notes: Code and data at https://github.com/richard-peng-xia/MMed-RAG

title: VRAG-RL: Empower Vision-Perception-Based RAG for Visually Rich Information Understanding via Iterative Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-trained vision-language agents with visual perception actions (crop, zoom) can iteratively refine retrieved evidence in multimodal RAG to better handle visually rich, noisy documents. | Integrating retrieval-quality rewards (NDCG-based) with model-based outcome rewards improves both retrieval precision and answer faithfulness in agentic multimodal RAG.
rationale: VRAG-RL is a NeurIPS 2025 paper that introduces an RL framework for visual RAG with a dedicated action space (search, region-select, crop, zoom) and a composite reward that explicitly penalizes retrieving irrelevant images. It directly addresses unreliable visual evidence by training the VLM to issue better queries and perceptually focus on information-dense regions, reducing noise in long visual contexts. It belongs in the modality chapter as a backbone vision RAG method and also supports the action-control narrative through RL-driven adaptive retrieval and perception.
caveat: Robustness claims are demonstrated on three visual document QA benchmarks rather than adversarial or poisoned-evidence settings, so its contribution to unreliable-evidence robustness is indirect (noise via retrieval failure rather than malicious or conflicting evidence).
notes: Code at Alibaba-NLP/VRAG; relevant baselines include Search-R1, ColPali, ViDoSeek.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
supports_claims: Vision-language models with late interaction enable end-to-end visual document retrieval that bypasses brittle OCR/layout pipelines for multimodal RAG. | The ViDoRe benchmark provides page-level retrieval evaluation across modalities, domains, and languages for visually rich documents. | Late-interaction multi-vector embeddings over image patches outperform text-only and contrastive VLM bi-encoders on visually rich document retrieval.
rationale: ColPali introduces a PaliGemma-based late-interaction retriever that embeds document page images directly and largely outperforms OCR/captioning pipelines and contrastive VLM bi-encoders on the new ViDoRe benchmark. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, this is a canonical backbone for visual/multimodal evidence construction and a reference benchmark for retrieval evaluation in long, visually rich documents. The paper also touches on interpretability via similarity maps and points to abstention/confidence as future work, making it suitable for the multimodal/scenario chapter.
caveat: Primary focus is retrieval performance and efficiency, not robustness to unreliable or adversarial evidence; reliability/abstention is only mentioned as future work.
notes: ICLR 2025 published; resources released under open licenses on HuggingFace.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Graph foundation models with query-dependent GNNs can mitigate noise and incompleteness in KG-indexed retrieval for RAG, enabling single-step multi-hop reasoning. | Pre-training a transferable GFM retriever on large-scale KGs yields generalization to unseen domain-specific RAG corpora without fine-tuning.
rationale: GFM-RAG proposes a graph foundation model retriever that explicitly targets noise and incompleteness in KG-based evidence structures, a core form of unreliable evidence in GraphRAG. It is a venue-linked (NeurIPS 2025) contribution that advances evidence construction for graph/KG scenario RAG, with strong empirical comparisons across multi-hop QA and domain-specific datasets. Placement in the modality/scenario section is appropriate as a backbone reference for graph_kg RAG, though it does not directly address adversarial poisoning or calibration/abstention.
caveat: The paper frames robustness narrowly as handling graph noise/incompleteness via GNN reasoning; it does not study adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflicts, or abstention under unreliable evidence.
notes: Project page https://rmanluo.github.io/gfm-rag indicates code/data availability.

title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
supports_claims: Graph-structured RAG can mitigate hallucination by retrieving connected subgraphs rather than treating triples in isolation. | Formulating subgraph retrieval as a Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree problem enables scalable, context-preserving evidence construction over textual graphs. | Combining GNN soft prompts with textualized retrieved subgraphs improves grounding and reduces invalid node/edge citations in graph QA.
rationale: G-Retriever introduces the first general retrieval-augmented generation framework for textual graphs, formulating subgraph retrieval as a PCST optimization to keep retrieved evidence connected, relevant, and bounded in size. The paper directly tackles hallucination by grounding generation in retrieved subgraphs and quantifies reductions in invalid nodes/edges, which is core evidence for a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence in the graph/KG scenario. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because it is a canonical NeurIPS-published graph RAG backbone with released code and datasets.
caveat: Retrieval is static and non-trainable, and hallucination evaluation is on a small manual sample (100 responses), so claims about robustness should not be overstated.
notes: GraphQA benchmark and PCST retrieval are reusable artifacts for graph RAG evaluation.

title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Graph/KG-augmented RAG with Personalized PageRank and LLM-based triple filtering improves retrieval robustness across factual, multi-hop, and discourse tasks compared with embedding-only RAG. | Recognition-memory style triple filtering and dense-sparse integration are effective mechanisms for reducing noise from LLM-generated KG structures in RAG pipelines.
rationale: HippoRAG 2 is an ICML 2025 graph/KG-augmented RAG method that combines OpenIE-extracted KGs, Personalized PageRank, dense-sparse integration of passages and phrases, and an LLM-based triple filter (recognition memory) to retrieve more reliable evidence across simple, multi-hop, and long-discourse QA. It is directly relevant to a robust RAG survey as a backbone graph-based retrieval method and as an example of evidence filtering to mitigate noisy KG triples. Main:modality is appropriate because the paper's central contribution is in the graph/KG RAG scenario, while also providing useful evidence-construction insights.
caveat: The paper does not explicitly target adversarial or unreliable-evidence robustness (e.g., poisoning, conflicts); claims about robustness are largely about cross-task consistency and corpus expansion.
notes: Code/data at github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG; useful as a representative KG-RAG method in the modality/scenario section.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
supports_claims: Heuristic multimodal RAG with fixed retrieval pipelines produces non-adaptive and overloaded queries that fail on dynamic, multi-hop, or cross-modal evidence needs. | Self-adaptive planning agents that decompose multimodal questions into sub-question chains with tool-selective retrieval improve robustness to unreliable or insufficient evidence. | Dyn-VQA provides a benchmark that stresses mRAG along rapidly changing answers, multimodal knowledge needs, and multi-hop reasoning.
rationale: The paper proposes Dyn-VQA, an ICLR 2025 benchmark explicitly designed to expose rigidity failures of heuristic multimodal RAG, and OmniSearch, a self-adaptive planning agent that dynamically chooses retrieval actions and tools based on intermediate evidence. It directly supports a robust-RAG survey on multimodal evidence construction and adaptive retrieval control, with quantitative comparisons against heuristic mRAG, generative search engines, and human baselines. Both dataset and code are open-sourced, strengthening reproducibility as a venue backbone for the multimodal/scenario chapter.
caveat: Evaluation relies on F1-Recall token overlap, which can over- or underestimate factuality; the agent loop can also over-retrieve or get stuck on grounding failures, limiting strong claims about full robustness.
notes: Strong fit for main:modality; also relevant to action_control and evaluation subsections.

title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
supports_claims: Retrieval-augmented generation can be extended to graph learning by constructing a toy-graph vector library and injecting retrieved subgraph features and labels through message-passing prompts. | Noise-aware prompt tuning with deliberately retrieved irrelevant or bottom-K subgraphs improves robustness against noisy retrieval in graph RAG. | Inverse importance sampling helps surface long-tail knowledge in the graph retrieval base, mitigating bias toward high-degree nodes.
rationale: RAGraph extends RAG to GNNs by building a key-value toy-graph base and using intra/inter graph propagation to integrate retrieved hidden embeddings and task-specific outputs, evaluated across node, edge, and graph tasks. Crucially for a robust-RAG survey, it includes explicit noise-handling mechanisms (inner-toy-graph noise and bottom-K toy-graph noise during training) and an inverse importance sampling strategy to mitigate long-tail bias, both directly relevant to unreliable-evidence robustness. The graph_kg scenario coverage and NeurIPS 2024 venue make it a strong main-text citation in the modality/scenario section. Overclaim risk is moderate: robustness evaluation is performance-centric and lacks dedicated adversarial or knowledge-conflict benchmarks.
caveat: Noise robustness is demonstrated via accuracy on standard benchmarks rather than dedicated unreliable-evidence stress tests, and the approach is specific to graph-structured retrieval rather than general RAG.
notes: NeurIPS 2024 paper with code at github.com/Artessay/RAGraph; relevant for graph-RAG section of modality scenarios.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
supports_claims: Reader robustness to retrieval noise, not retriever quality, is the primary determinant of RAG stability and scalability across configurations. | Systematic evaluation across retrieval depths reveals two distinct reader behaviors (improve-then-plateau vs peak-then-decline), motivating stability/scalability metrics (RSS, RSC) for diagnosing RAG reliability. | Prompt-based relevance instructions provide inconsistent noise mitigation and cannot substitute for reader-level noise robustness.
rationale: RAGGED introduces a systematic evaluation framework with two new diagnostic metrics (RSS, RSC) for assessing RAG performance under realistic noisy retrieval across multiple retrievers, readers, and datasets (NQ, HotpotQA, BioASQ). It directly addresses unreliable-evidence robustness by showing that reader noise sensitivity—rather than retriever quality—drives downstream stability, and that retrieval-side fixes like reranking or prompting are insufficient. As an ICML 2025 paper with released code/data, it fits naturally as a backbone citation in the evaluation section of a robust-RAG survey.
caveat: Scope is limited to text QA with F1-based metrics and uses naturally retrieved noise rather than adversarial/poisoned evidence, so claims about full unreliable-evidence robustness should not be overstated.
notes: Scenario metadata says table_structured but the paper does not focus on tables; it spans open-domain and biomedical QA.

title: TableRAG: Million-Token Table Understanding with Language Models
supports_claims: Schema-plus-cell retrieval with query expansion enables scalable table-grounded RAG over million-token tables, mitigating context-length and lost-in-the-middle issues. | Frequency-aware cell encoding and budgeted retrieval provide a tractable evidence-construction strategy for large structured tables. | Dedicated table RAG benchmarks (ArcadeQA, BirdQA, synthetic TabFact) expose scalability and retrieval-quality gaps in prior table prompting methods.
rationale: TableRAG is a venue-backbone NeurIPS 2024 paper that adapts RAG to large-scale table understanding via schema and cell retrieval with query expansion and an encoding budget. It is directly relevant to the survey's modality/scenario chapter on table-structured RAG and supports evidence-construction discussions about retrieval precision/recall and prompt compression under unreliable or oversized evidence. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because it is one of the canonical large-table RAG frameworks and introduces useful benchmarks for evaluation.
caveat: Focuses on QA accuracy and retrieval F1 rather than on adversarial or noisy-evidence robustness; claims about unreliable-evidence handling should not be overstated.

title: Retrieval Augmented Visual Question Answering with Outside Knowledge
supports_claims: Joint training of dense retriever and generator in multimodal OK-VQA can outperform two-step pipelines and standard RAG when pseudo-relevance labels are noisy. | Diagnostic metrics (HSR/FSR) and analysis show how unreliable pseudo-relevance signals can mislead retriever training and how combining model predictions with relevance labels mitigates this.
rationale: This EMNLP 2022 paper introduces RA-VQA, a joint retrieval-generation framework for OK-VQA with vision-to-language transformation and a loss that combines pseudo-relevance with model predictions to avoid misleading document scoring. It directly engages with unreliable evidence concerns by showing how standard RAG loss can upvote irrelevant documents and proposes diagnostic metrics (HSR/FSR, PRRecall) to analyze retrieval-generation interaction. As a venue-backbone multimodal RAG paper, it fits the modality/scenario chapter and also provides secondary evidence-use insights relevant to the survey.
caveat: Scope is limited to OK-VQA/FVQA with Google Search/KG corpora; the 'unreliable evidence' framing is implicit through pseudo-relevance analysis rather than adversarial or corrupted retrieval settings.
notes: Code repo URL appears truncated in extraction; full repo is github.com/LinWeizheDragon/Retrieval-Augmented-Visual-Question-Answering.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic  Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
supports_claims: Two-stage semantic filtering combining cluster-based and entity-intent-relation graph reasoning can defend RAG against corpus poisoning while preserving useful evidence. | Conflict-aware filtering that cross-checks retrieved documents against query intent, other retrieved evidence, and the model's internal knowledge mitigates knowledge conflicts in RAG generation.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper proposes SeCon-RAG, a two-stage defense that combines semantic/clustering filtering with conflict-aware filtering using an Entity-Intent-Relation Extractor to handle corpus poisoning and prompt injection. It directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable evidence by tackling both adversarial contamination and internal/external knowledge conflicts, with experiments across five LLMs and three QA datasets against PoisonedRAG and PIA. It is a strong main-text citation for the security/integrity strand and also informs evidence construction and conflict resolution discussions.
caveat: Evaluated only on open-domain QA datasets and relies on LLM-based semantic extraction plus a small manually verified clean reference set, which adds runtime overhead and may not generalize to multimodal or domain-specific RAG.
notes: Scenario tag in metadata (table_structured) does not match the paper, which targets general open-domain QA defense.

title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Subgraph-based KG retrieval with flexible size and structural encoding improves evidence coverage and reduces hallucinations in KG-RAG. | Adjustable retrieval size matters: more triples help capable LLMs but degrade smaller LLMs, reflecting the model-evidence capacity tradeoff. | Knowledge-grounded prompting over retrieved subgraphs improves truth-grounded QA and supports abstention when evidence is insufficient.
rationale: SubgraphRAG is an ICLR 2025 KG-based RAG framework that uses a lightweight MLP with parallel triple scoring and Directional Distance Encoding to retrieve flexible-size subgraphs, then prompts unfine-tuned LLMs to reason over them. It directly contributes to the graph/KG scenario in robust RAG, addressing evidence sufficiency, irrelevant-context degradation, hallucination reduction, and explicit refusal behavior when evidence is missing. Placement in main:modality is appropriate as it is a representative venue-backbone for KG-RAG and also offers insights on evidence-size tradeoffs and grounding. Overclaim risk is modest since results focus on WebQSP/CWQ KGQA benchmarks.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to two Freebase-based KGQA benchmarks; robustness to noisy or adversarial KG evidence is not directly tested.

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Systematic ablation across RAG pipeline modules (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization) identifies best-performing configurations and quantifies performance-latency trade-offs. | Fine-tuning the generator with a mix of relevant and randomly-sampled documents improves robustness to irrelevant retrieved context while preserving use of relevant evidence. | RAG workflows can be extended to multimodal settings via text2image/image2text retrieval and a retrieval-as-generation strategy for groundedness.
rationale: The paper performs a systematic search over RAG workflow choices and includes an explicit robustness experiment showing that mixing gold and random documents during generator fine-tuning yields models more robust to irrelevant context. This directly supports survey claims on evidence construction, summarization for noise reduction, and training-time strategies for unreliable evidence. It is venue-linked (EMNLP 2024) with open code and serves as a backbone reference for the evidence-construction perspective. Overclaim risk is modest since the best practices are empirically derived on specific datasets and may not generalize universally.
caveat: Best-practice claims are empirically tuned on selected QA/reasoning datasets and a specific generator (Llama2-7B), so generalization to adversarial or domain-shifted unreliable-evidence settings is not fully established.
notes: Multimodal extension is brief; main contribution is workflow-level best practices and robustness-oriented fine-tuning.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Knowledge-graph-indexed retrieval with Personalized PageRank enables single-step multi-hop evidence aggregation, improving robustness when relevant evidence is dispersed across passages. | Neurobiologically inspired long-term memory structures provide a scalable alternative to iterative retrieval for integrating new evidence into LLMs.
rationale: HippoRAG is a NeurIPS 2024 paper that constructs an OpenIE-derived KG as a hippocampal index and uses Personalized PageRank for multi-hop retrieval, significantly outperforming standard RAG baselines on MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it represents a major venue-backbone method in the graph/KG-augmented retrieval and long-term memory lineage, directly addressing evidence construction for integrating knowledge across passages. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because the core mechanism is structurally graph-based, though it also has clear evidence_construction relevance.
caveat: Robustness to noisy or adversarial evidence is not the paper's focus; error analysis notes OpenIE/NER errors propagate, and scalability beyond benchmark-size corpora remains unvalidated.
notes: Could alternatively be placed at main:evidence; graph_kg scenario_hit aligns with agent_memory_tool framing in metadata.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Iterative chain-of-retrieval with dynamic query reformulation mitigates failures of single-step retrieval on complex multi-hop queries. | Test-time scaling strategies (greedy, best-of-N, tree search) and learning-to-stop allow adaptive compute allocation based on query complexity and retriever quality. | Trained iterative retrieval pipelines remain robust across retrievers of varying strength (E5-large, E5-base, BM25).
rationale: CoRAG explicitly targets unreliable single-step retrieval by training an LLM via rejection-sampled retrieval chains to decompose queries and reformulate when retrieval fails. It provides concrete mechanisms (greedy, best-of-N, tree search, learn-to-stop) and demonstrates robustness across different retrievers and weak-to-strong generalization, all directly relevant to robust RAG under noisy evidence. Published at NeurIPS 2025 with code/data released, it is a strong main-citation backbone for the evidence-construction and action-control sections.
caveat: Focuses on short-answer QA (multi-hop QA, KILT) and does not directly address adversarial/poisoned evidence or long-form generation; robustness claims are about retriever quality, not malicious or conflicting evidence.
notes: Could alternatively be placed in main:control given the test-time scaling and learn-to-stop contributions.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
supports_claims: RL-trained adaptive search intensity scaling enables LLMs to escalate retrieval frequency and depth in noisy real-web environments, improving robustness over fixed prompting or SFT pipelines. | Training and evaluating iterative RAG on open-web noisy sources surfaces conflict resolution, verification/denoising, and reflection behaviors that clean Wiki benchmarks fail to elicit.
rationale: DeepDiver proposes an RL framework (GRPO over iterative RAG) that learns when and how aggressively to search, directly targeting unreliable/noisy/conflicting web evidence rather than clean Wikipedia. It introduces WebPuzzle, a benchmark explicitly designed to require evidence gathering, conflict resolution, verification/denoising, and reflective correction, which maps cleanly to the survey's robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence theme. Suitable as a main_cite under action_control (adaptive retrieval/routing) with a secondary tie to evaluation. Overclaim risk: results are primarily Chinese 7B-scale and rely on LLM-as-judge graders.
caveat: Evaluation is heavily Chinese-centric, uses LLM-based graders, and reward design choices may confound the claimed emergence of search-intensity scaling.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 venue-linked; code/data not yet released at submission.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
supports_claims: Reliability-aware document selection via Maximum Independent Set over a contradiction graph provides provably robust defense against corpus poisoning and prompt injection in RAG. | Weighted sample-and-aggregate frameworks leveraging document ranking/weights enable scalable robustness against adversarial retrieval corruption while preserving benign utility. | Defense-in-depth strategies that exploit retriever reliability signals outperform position-agnostic robust RAG baselines on both short-form QA and long-form generation.
rationale: This NeurIPS 2025 paper proposes ReliabilityRAG, which constructs a contradiction graph over retrieved documents (via NLI on isolated answers) and selects a rank-aware Maximum Independent Set to filter malicious passages, with provable robustness guarantees and a weighted sample-and-aggregate variant for scalability. It directly targets unreliable evidence (corpus poisoning, prompt injection) and benchmarks against RobustRAG, AstuteRAG, and InstructRAG on RQA/NQ/TQA/Bio, making it a backbone reference for the security/integrity dimension of robust RAG. Main-text security placement is appropriate because it advances both the mechanism (consistency-based filtering with reliability priors) and the evaluation lineage for defended RAG.
caveat: Robustness guarantees depend on NLI quality and the assumption that malicious answers diverge enough to be detected as contradictions; effectiveness on truly adaptive context-aware attacks and very long-form generation remains less explored.
notes: Code release promised post-acceptance; only a partial HuggingFace URL signal extracted.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
supports_claims: Domain-specific RAG benchmarks (e.g., MIRAGE for medicine) reveal that retriever/corpus/LLM choices have large and task-dependent effects on answer accuracy. | Medical RAG exhibits log-linear scaling with the number of retrieved snippets and a 'lost-in-the-middle' effect on the position of the ground-truth snippet, highlighting context-use robustness issues. | Combining heterogeneous corpora and fusing retrievers (e.g., RRF) tends to improve robustness across diverse medical QA tasks.
rationale: The paper proposes MIRAGE, a benchmark of 7,663 medical QA items, and MedRAG, a toolkit spanning 5 corpora, 4 retrievers, and 6 LLMs, enabling systematic evaluation of RAG component choices. It documents log-linear scaling with retrieved-snippet count and a 'lost-in-the-middle' phenomenon in medical RAG, both directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable/noisy evidence. As a venue-published (ACL Findings 2024) benchmark with open code and data covering a high-stakes domain, it fits main-text evaluation citation, particularly in the domain/scenario section.
caveat: The work focuses on multi-choice medical QA with vanilla prepend-RAG, so its conclusions may not transfer to open-ended generation, adversarial/poisoned evidence, or non-medical domains.
notes: ACL Findings 2024; strong fit for evaluation and domain-scenario discussion in survey.

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
supports_claims: Dense retrieval systems in domain-specific RAG (medical and legal Q&A) are vulnerable to universal poisoning attacks where attacker-crafted documents are reliably retrieved for targeted queries across diverse corpora, retrievers, and query sets. | An orthogonal augmentation property of dense retrievers explains why concatenating targeted content to queries preserves high similarity, motivating Mahalanobis-distance-based detection that outperforms L2-norm baselines for filtering poisoned documents.
rationale: This ICML 2025 paper systematically demonstrates RAG corpus poisoning vulnerabilities across 225 setups in medical Q&A (and legal Q&A), introduces a theoretical explanation via orthogonal augmentation, and proposes a shrinkage-regularized Mahalanobis distance defense with near-perfect detection rates. It directly contributes to the security/integrity dimension of robust RAG under unreliable evidence, with a strong domain-specific (biomed/legal) scenario focus. Placement in the security section is appropriate because it spans both attack characterization and defense design.
caveat: Defense assumes access to a clean anchor set of documents tied to protected queries, and PubMed subset rather than full corpus is used; generalization to non-medical adversarial scenarios is only lightly explored.
notes: Strong venue-backbone citation for the security/poisoning subsection; also relevant as a domain-specific (biomed/legal) case study.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Context Compression and Selective Augmentation
supports_claims: Context compression of retrieved documents can filter irrelevant evidence and reduce LM distraction while maintaining task performance. | Selective augmentation (returning an empty summary when retrieved evidence is unhelpful) is an effective mechanism for handling unreliable retrieval results. | Compressors trained with end-task signals can outperform off-the-shelf summarization for RAG and transfer across different LMs.
rationale: RECOMP proposes both extractive and abstractive compressors that summarize retrieved documents before prepending them to the LM input, with explicit selective augmentation (empty summary) when retrieved evidence is irrelevant or harmful. This directly addresses two key axes of robust RAG under unreliable evidence: filtering noisy/irrelevant retrieval and abstaining from augmentation when retrieval hurts. The analyses on faithfulness, comprehensiveness, and how models copy spans even when answer is absent are particularly useful for the evidence-construction chapter, and the work is a venue-backbone for context-compression lineage. Placement under main:evidence is appropriate, with possible cross-reference to action_control for the selective augmentation aspect.
caveat: Selective augmentation here is binary (summary vs. empty) and tied to specific base LMs; transfer experiments show limited generalization for QA across LM families, so claims about general robustness should be tempered.
notes: ICLR 2024, code at github.com/carriex/recomp; relevant for both evidence construction (compression/filtering) and adaptive/selective augmentation discussions.

title: RAG-QA Arena: Evaluating Domain Robustness for Long-form Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
supports_claims: Long-form RAG-QA evaluation requires coherent multi-document reference answers and pairwise LLM-judge protocols that align with human judgment | Cross-domain robustness of RAG-QA systems can be benchmarked via LFRQA across seven domains, revealing that top LLMs only win 41.3% against human-annotated references
rationale: The paper introduces LFRQA, a multi-domain human-annotated long-form RAG-QA dataset, and RAG-QA Arena, a pairwise LLM-judge evaluation framework that handles conflicting information from multiple documents. It directly contributes to evaluation protocols for robust RAG under unreliable evidence by addressing domain shift, multi-document aggregation, and answer coherence under conflicts. Placement in main:evaluation is appropriate because it is a venue-published benchmark with code/data that a robust RAG survey would cite for evaluation methodology and cross-domain robustness measurement.
caveat: Focuses on text-only QA evaluation; reliability framing centers on cross-domain generalization and reference quality rather than adversarial or poisoned evidence.
notes: EMNLP 2024 main conference; artifacts at github.com/awslabs/rag-qa-arena.

title: LaRA: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Long-Context LLMs – No Silver Bullet for LC or RAG Routing
supports_claims: Benchmarks comparing RAG vs long-context LLMs reveal that the optimal choice depends on model strength, context length, task type, and retrieval characteristics, with no universal winner. | RAG provides robustness advantages for hallucination detection and mitigates the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon compared to feeding full long contexts. | Prior RAG-vs-LC benchmarks suffer from insufficient context length, data leakage, truncation issues, and unreliable automated metrics, motivating more rigorous evaluation protocols.
rationale: LaRA is an ICML 2025 benchmark with 2326 cases across four QA tasks (location, reasoning, comparison, hallucination detection) and three long-context types, designed to rigorously compare RAG and long-context LLMs across 11 models. It directly informs survey discussions on evaluation protocols for robust RAG and on action-control style routing decisions between RAG and LC under varying conditions. The hallucination detection task and lost-in-the-middle analysis make it directly relevant to robustness under unreliable evidence. Main:evaluation placement is appropriate given its benchmark contribution and methodological critique of prior evaluation pipelines.
caveat: Scope is limited to English QA over long documents and uses GPT-4o as judge, so generalization to multilingual, open-ended, or adversarial evidence settings is not directly established.
notes: PMLR v267 ICML 2025 paper; code and data available at github.com/Alibaba-NLP/LaRA.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
supports_claims: Self-reflection routing between RAG and long-context LLMs can reduce cost while maintaining accuracy comparable to full long-context processing. | RAG failures cluster around multi-step reasoning, general or complex queries, and implicit questions requiring holistic context understanding. | Comprehensive benchmarking shows long-context LLMs often outperform RAG but at substantially higher token cost, motivating adaptive evidence-use strategies.
rationale: The paper benchmarks RAG vs long-context LLMs across nine datasets and proposes Self-Route, which uses LLM self-reflection to decide whether retrieved chunks suffice or whether to fall back to full long-context processing. This is directly relevant to action control / adaptive retrieval under potentially insufficient evidence and provides a useful failure taxonomy for RAG (multi-step, general, complex, implicit queries). Placement in main:control is appropriate because the routing mechanism exemplifies a self-reflective abstention/escalation strategy central to robust RAG.
caveat: Self-reflection routing assumes LLM is well-calibrated about answerability; the paper notes performance drops for Gemini and acknowledges dataset leakage and synthetic-data artifact issues that limit generality.
notes: EMNLP 2024 Industry Track; code link is only to needle-in-haystack repo, no Self-Route artifact released.

title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
supports_claims: Graph-augmented RAG with Personalized PageRank and LLM-based triple filtering improves robustness across factual, sense-making, and multi-hop associative retrieval tasks. | Recognition-memory style triple filtering can reduce noise from retrieved structured evidence and balance phrase-level versus passage-level signals in KG-based retrieval. | Non-parametric continual learning frameworks built on graph indexing remain stable as the corpus grows, but multi-hop performance degrades faster than single-hop performance.
rationale: HippoRAG 2 is a venue-published (ICML 2025) framework that integrates KG construction, dense-sparse passage integration, and an LLM-based triple filter (recognition memory) to improve retrieval quality and reduce irrelevant evidence in multi-hop and continual-learning RAG settings. It directly contributes to evidence construction and noise filtering, which are core themes for robust RAG under unreliable evidence, and it fits the agent/memory scenario for the survey. Placement in main:modality is appropriate because it serves as a backbone example of memory-oriented RAG; an overclaim risk is treating it as a security/poisoning defense, which it does not address.
caveat: The paper does not target adversarial poisoning or prompt injection; its 'unreliable evidence' handling is limited to LLM-based relevance filtering and graph weighting rather than malicious or conflicting evidence.
notes: ICML 2025 PMLR v267; code at github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG.

title: LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering
supports_claims: Dual-perspective RAG with a global information extractor and CoT-guided filter improves evidence quality and reduces noise for long-context multi-hop QA. | Mapping retrieved chunks back to source paragraphs preserves contextual structure and mitigates the lost-in-the-middle problem in long-context RAG.
rationale: LongRAG proposes a plug-and-play RAG paradigm combining a hybrid retriever, an LLM-augmented information extractor, and a CoT-guided filter that explicitly targets noise filtering and incomplete-evidence problems in long-context multi-hop QA. It directly addresses unreliable evidence symptoms (lost-in-the-middle, low evidence density, chunk truncation) and provides ablations isolating the contributions of extractor versus filter, which is relevant to a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence. Placement under main:evidence fits because its primary contributions are about evidence construction and filtering rather than calibration or attack defense.
caveat: Evaluation is restricted to three multi-hop QA datasets from LongBench and to one-time retrieval; robustness to adversarial or poisoned evidence is not directly studied.
notes: EMNLP 2024 main proceedings; code and data publicly available.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG
supports_claims: Visual RAG can mitigate high-resolution image perception challenges in MLLMs by retrieving query-relevant image crops while preserving spatial layout. | Adaptive retrieval control using model confidence and retrieval scores (RE-Search) can dynamically determine the number of evidence units needed per task type. | Preserving relative spatial relationships among retrieved evidence is critical for cross-instance perception tasks, illustrating evidence-construction principles for multimodal RAG.
rationale: The paper introduces RAP, a training-free visual RAG framework that retrieves image crops, uses a Spatial-Awareness Layout to preserve positional relationships, and applies an A*-style RE-Search guided by model confidence to adaptively choose how many crops to retain. This directly contributes to a robust-RAG survey's multimodal/scenario chapter by showing how evidence construction and confidence-based adaptive retrieval interact in vision settings. Published at ICML 2025 with code available, making it a solid main citation for visual RAG and adaptive evidence selection.
caveat: Focus is on HR image perception accuracy rather than adversarial/noisy evidence robustness; the 'unreliable evidence' framing is implicit (irrelevant crops) rather than explicitly addressing poisoning or conflicting evidence.
notes: Strong candidate for the multimodal/vision RAG section; also useful as a case study for confidence-driven adaptive retrieval in vision.

title: Reliable Decision‑Making via Calibration‑Oriented Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Calibration-aware reranking in RAG can mitigate overconfidence introduced by retrieved evidence and align predicted confidence with downstream decision correctness. | Training a forecasting function with temperature-conditioned soft labels enables adaptive document selection and optional query reformulation when retrieved evidence is insufficient.
rationale: The paper proposes CalibRAG, which trains a forecasting function to predict whether a user decision based on a retrieved document will be correct, then reranks documents by this calibrated confidence and optionally reformulates the query when confidence is below threshold. This directly addresses robust RAG under unreliable evidence by tackling overconfidence on irrelevant or low-utility retrieved documents and by introducing adaptive retrieval/abstention-like behavior. It fits main:control as a calibration and adaptive-retrieval lineage paper, with empirical comparisons against uncertainty calibration, reranking, and SelfRAG baselines across general and medical QA. Overclaim risk is moderate since improvements depend on synthetic supervision from a surrogate user model.
caveat: Calibration labels are derived from a GPT-4o-mini-judged surrogate user model rather than real human decisions, which may bias the forecasting function.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper; scenario tag long_context_doc in metadata is loose since experiments are standard QA plus medical QA.

title: Influence Guided Context Selection for Effective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Inference-time data valuation can quantify per-context contribution to RAG generation quality, integrating query relevance, list-level uniqueness, and generator alignment for noise filtering. | Learned surrogate models can approximate oracle context-influence scores to enable label-free, low-latency context selection that improves robustness to noisy retrieval.
rationale: The paper proposes Contextual Influence (CI) value and a hierarchical surrogate model (CSM) for selecting high-quality contexts in RAG, explicitly targeting irrelevant and noisy retrieved evidence across 8 knowledge-intensive NLP tasks with Llama3 and Qwen2.5. It directly supports the evidence-construction line of a robust RAG survey by reframing context selection as inference-time data valuation and offering a configuration-free positive-CI selection rule. Placement in main:evidence is appropriate because it provides a concrete mechanism for shielding generators from unreliable evidence. Caveat: experiments are text-only on standard QA/fact-checking benchmarks, not multimodal despite the collection tag.
caveat: Despite being tagged vision_multimodal, the paper is text-only on standard NLP benchmarks and requires task-specific CSM training, limiting cross-task generalization claims.
notes: Scenario metadata mismatch: paper is not multimodal; it addresses noise-robust context selection for text RAG.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
supports_claims: FaithEval provides a fine-grained benchmark for evaluating LLM faithfulness under unanswerable, inconsistent, and counterfactual contexts that simulate unreliable retrieved evidence in RAG. | Even state-of-the-art LLMs struggle to remain faithful to noisy contexts, and larger models do not necessarily exhibit improved faithfulness. | Task-specific abstention instructions can induce sycophantic degradation on normal contexts, highlighting a tension between robustness and routine performance.
rationale: The paper introduces a 4.9K-sample benchmark explicitly targeting RAG-style unreliable evidence: missing information (unanswerable), conflicting documents (inconsistent), and counterfactual fabrications. It evaluates 18 modern open and proprietary LLMs with a rigorous LLM-judge plus human validation pipeline, providing direct diagnostics on faithfulness hallucination under noisy retrieval. This is a venue-backbone evaluation contribution for a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence and naturally belongs in the evaluation section.
caveat: Contexts are LLM-synthesized rather than from real retrieval pipelines, and the inconsistent context construction uses fabricated counter-evidence which may differ from genuine retrieval noise distributions.
