title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
supports_claims: Self-reflective reflection tokens enable adaptive on-demand retrieval and self-critique over retrieved passages, improving robustness to irrelevant or unsupported evidence. | Fine-grained critique tokens (IsRel, IsSup, IsUse) provide a controllable mechanism to enforce evidence grounding and citation faithfulness at inference time. | Segment-level beam search guided by reflection token probabilities allows test-time customization of trade-offs between citation precision and fluency.
rationale: Self-RAG trains an LM to emit special reflection tokens that decide when to retrieve, judge passage relevance, assess support, and rate utility, enabling adaptive retrieval and self-critique. This directly addresses unreliable evidence by filtering irrelevant passages and grounding generations in supported content, with measurable gains in citation precision/recall. It is a venue-backbone ICLR 2024 paper that any survey on robust RAG should cite under action control and adaptive retrieval, also touching evidence use/faithfulness.
caveat: Critic relies on GPT-4 distilled labels and Llama2 base; reflection token accuracy and adaptive thresholding may not generalize to all domains or modalities.

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Mid-to-deep FFN layers are mechanistically implicated in unfaithful RAG generation, and selectively suppressing their activation can reduce reliance on parametric memory and improve contextual faithfulness. | A consistency-filtered benchmark (CoFaithfulQA) combined with knowledge-preference optimization enables evaluation and mitigation of knowledge-conflict failures in RAG.
rationale: The paper identifies Unfaithfulness-Associated FFNs via correlation and causal NLL interventions, then proposes a suppression-plus-adaptation framework (ParamMute) that calibrates models toward retrieved evidence over parametric memory. It also releases CoFaithfulQA and evaluates on ConFiQA/FaithEval, making it directly relevant to the model_evidence_use chapter of a robust RAG survey on unreliable evidence and knowledge conflict. Placement in main:model is appropriate because it offers both a mechanistic explanation and a method lineage for faithfulness control.
caveat: Experiments focus on QA-style text RAG with a single backbone family for analysis; generalization to multimodal or agentic RAG settings is not directly demonstrated.
notes: NeurIPS 2025 venue confirmed; code at OpenBMB/ParamMute.

title: Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG: Overcoming Challenges for Long Inputs in RAG
supports_claims: Increasing retrieved passage count for long-context LLMs follows an inverted-U pattern due to hard negatives, demonstrating the unreliability of larger retrieval contexts. | Retrieval reordering plus RAG-specific fine-tuning (implicit robustness and explicit relevance reasoning) improves robustness to hard negatives in long-context RAG. | Stronger retrievers can produce harder negatives that more severely mislead the generator, complicating the use of precision/recall as adequacy metrics.
rationale: This ICLR 2025 paper systematically diagnoses how hard negatives degrade long-context RAG performance and proposes a training-free reordering method plus two fine-tuning strategies (implicit robustness and explicit intermediate-reasoning relevance identification). It directly speaks to the survey's themes of unreliable evidence (noisy/hard-negative passages), evidence ordering, and robust generator behavior in a long-context scenario. The main:modality placement fits its long-context RAG focus, and it also offers strong cross-cutting evidence for evidence-construction and model-evidence-use sections.
caveat: Experiments focus on QA-style benchmarks with Wikipedia/PubMed corpora and a limited set of retrievers/LLMs; some claims (e.g., why Gemini-1.5-Pro is more robust) remain speculative.
notes: Repo links in PDF are to third-party training/inference tools (axolotl, vllm), not an explicit code release for the method.

title: Training Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering through Backtracking Correction
supports_claims: Training methods that reformulate multi-document RAG as a multi-step decision process with self-correction can improve robustness to noisy retrieved documents. | Backtracking-style stepwise preference optimization reduces reliance on costly chain-of-thought annotations while improving the LLM's ability to assess document relevance. | Chain-supervised tuning and label-supervised tuning each have limitations when handling unreliable retrieved evidence in open-domain QA.
rationale: The paper proposes Backtracking Correction, a stepwise RL training approach that teaches LLMs to sequentially assess retrieved documents and self-correct errors, explicitly targeting noise robustness in RAG. It contrasts Label-Supervised Tuning, Chain-Supervised Tuning, and its method on four open-domain QA benchmarks with a real retriever, showing improved discrimination of relevant vs irrelevant documents. This is directly relevant to a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence as a model-side training method for evidence use, and code/data are released. Placement in main:model is appropriate because the contribution is mechanistic (training scheme), not just an evaluation or benchmark.
caveat: Evaluation is limited to open-domain QA with Wikipedia and Contriever; robustness to adversarial or poisoned evidence and multimodal/long-context settings is not directly tested.
notes: ICLR 2025 paper with GitHub artifact; scenario tag long_context_doc is loose since the focus is multi-document open-domain QA rather than truly long-context.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
supports_claims: Self-synthesized rationales can teach LMs to explicitly denoise noisy retrieved contexts, improving accuracy and verifiability over implicit denoising baselines. | Explicit rationale-based denoising remains robust as the number of retrieved documents (and noise ratio) grows, outperforming vanilla SFT and Self-RAG style baselines. | Instruction-following LMs can synthesize generalizable denoising supervision without GPT-4 or human annotation, transferring across QA tasks and even to code generation.
rationale: InstructRAG introduces a self-synthesized rationale framework where an instruction-tuned LM explains how the ground-truth answer is derived from potentially noisy retrieved documents, then uses these rationales for ICL or SFT. It directly targets the unreliable-evidence problem central to the survey, providing both a method and analysis (noise robustness curves, OOD transfer, attention visualization) that fit the model-evidence-use perspective. As an ICLR 2025 paper with released code and consistent gains across five knowledge-intensive benchmarks, it serves as a venue-backbone citation for the section on explicit denoising and faithful use of noisy contexts.
caveat: Despite the scenario tag, the paper is text-only QA and not truly multimodal; claims about general robustness rest on pattern-matching metrics and a single retriever per dataset.
notes: Scenario hit of vision_multimodal appears to be a metadata artifact; the actual contribution is in textual long-context QA RAG.

title: Measuring and Enhancing Trustworthiness of LLMs in RAG through Grounded Attributions and Learning to Refuse
supports_claims: Alignment-based learning-to-refuse improves RAG robustness when retrieved evidence is insufficient by reducing over-responsiveness and hallucinated grounding. | Holistic trustworthiness metrics combining grounded refusal, answer calibration, and citation precision/recall isolate LLM behavior from retriever quality and expose parametric-knowledge leakage.
rationale: The paper introduces TRUST-SCORE (a metric covering grounded refusal, answer correctness calibrated to retrieved docs, and citation groundedness) and TRUST-ALIGN (a DPO-based alignment over 19K paired samples targeting five hallucination types). It directly tackles robust RAG under unreliable evidence by training models to refuse when documents are insufficient and to ground citations, evaluated across LLaMA/Qwen/Phi families on ASQA/QAMPARI/ELI5/ExpertQA. Placement in main:control fits because the central mechanistic claim is action control via learn-to-refuse alignment, with strong secondary evaluation contributions.
caveat: Scenario tag in metadata (code_math_symbolic) is misleading; the paper is general factoid/long-form QA rather than code/math, and the answerability label depends on NLI quality.
notes: Could also be cited under main:evaluation for TRUST-SCORE; venue is ICLR 2025 with public code at declare-lab/trust-align.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
supports_claims: Unifying context ranking and answer generation via instruction tuning can filter noisy retrieved evidence and improve RAG robustness under imperfect retrieval. | Reranking with a small amount of ranking data can outperform dedicated reranker models and improve recall of relevant contexts in knowledge-intensive QA and biomedical RAG. | Selecting top-k contexts involves a recall-noise tradeoff that motivates integrated ranking within RAG pipelines.
rationale: RankRAG instruction-tunes a single LLM to jointly rerank retrieved passages and generate answers, directly addressing the problem of noisy/irrelevant retrieved evidence that destabilizes RAG. It empirically demonstrates the tradeoff between top-k size and irrelevant context noise (Figure 1) and shows that integrated ranking improves robustness across nine general-domain and five biomedical benchmarks, including under weak retrievers. As a NeurIPS 2024 paper contributing a unified retrieve-rerank-generate pipeline, it is a strong venue-backbone citation for the evidence construction section of the survey.
caveat: Focuses on single-round retrieval and improving recall; does not directly address adversarial poisoning, abstention, or calibration under unreliable evidence.
notes: Strong evidence-construction lineage paper; useful for discussion of context filtering and recall-noise tradeoff.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
supports_claims: Token-level fusion between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence can be theoretically decomposed into benefit (distribution completion) and detriment (distribution contradiction). | The actual effect of RAG on each token can be predicted from representation similarity without training or external utility evaluators, enabling adaptive token-level use of retrieved evidence. | Training-free collaborative decoding between pure LLM and RAG improves robustness to noisy retrieved passages across QA and long-form tasks.
rationale: This ICLR 2025 paper formalizes RAG as a distribution fusion between LLM knowledge and retrieved texts, decomposing it into benefit and detriment terms tied to knowledge completion vs. contradiction, and proves these can be compared via representation similarity at token level. The proposed Tok-RAG performs collaborative pure-LLM/RAG decoding to preserve useful evidence and discard misleading content, directly addressing robustness under unreliable retrieval. It is a strong mechanistic and theoretical anchor for the survey's discussion of how LLMs should consume potentially noisy evidence, justifying a main-text citation in the model/evidence-use section. Risk: the theoretical claims rely on HMM-style latent-variable assumptions and layer-wise heuristics that may not hold for all architectures.
caveat: Theory rests on strong latent-variable/HMM assumptions and the practical method depends on heuristics for locating the 'distribution fusion' layer.
notes: Although metadata tags scenario as code_math_symbolic, the paper is a general RAG method evaluated across QA, dialogue, code, slot filling, and LM tasks.

title: Speculative RAG: Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation through Drafting
supports_claims: Multi-perspective document subset sampling with parallel drafting mitigates position bias in long-context RAG | Verifier scoring over draft rationales filters unreliable drafts without instruction-tuning the generalist LM
rationale: The paper proposes a draft-then-verify RAG framework that clusters retrieved documents, generates diverse drafts with a small specialist, and verifies via a generalist LM using rationale-based confidence scoring. This directly contributes to evidence construction and reliability under noisy multi-document retrieval, with clear relevance to robust RAG.
caveat: Focused on QA accuracy and latency, not adversarial or poisoned evidence settings.
